Hi Elaine / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our end and recommended next steps to validate model fit for the semantic search use case you showed (product detail + legacy docs + customer reviews):

Summary / hypothesis
- Primary objective: improve semantic recall for long-tail product queries and upstream recommendation signal while keeping index size and latency within current constraints.
- Current metric focus: MRR and recall@10 on your curated eval set. We recommend adding a P@5 check for the short query set.

Recommended models & dimensionality tradeoffs
- Recommendation A (accuracy-first): text-embedding-3-large (2048d) — best for recall and robustness to vocabulary drift.
- Recommendation B (cost/latency-balanced): redwood-emb-quant-v2 (1024d, 8-bit quantized) — ~20-30% lower cost with small drop in recall for long-tail queries.
- Dimensionality note: higher dims (1536-2048) generally help recall on noisy product descriptions, but increase index size and slightly increase similarity search latency.

Benchmarks & artifacts
- Attached: embeddings-benchmarks.csv (sample metrics on your public dataset + synthetic drift tests).
- Prompt set / eval queries: prompt-set-v1.txt attached.
- Eval notebook & shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1a2b3c-eval-notebook

Quality/regression concerns
- We saw potential regression on short, brand-specific queries when switching from your current embeddings to higher-dim models; this is addressable by a blended index or reranker.
- Drift: will want to run periodic similarity drift checks (cosine shift & class-wise recall) — we included a short checklist in the notebook.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) You: share a 2-5k sample of your search traffic + eval labels (or a representative subset).
2) Redwood: run model-fit evaluation (MRR, recall@K, latency/cost estimates) across 2 models (text-embedding-3-large, redwood-emb-quant-v2) and return a short report (3 business days).
3) Joint call: review results and decide on pilot config (blended index vs single model).

Please let me know the best email or Drive folder to drop the ingestion instructions and whether next Wednesday (10/20) 11am PT works for a 30-min results review.

Hi Elaine —

Quick answers to the data-team questions below, plus a short checklist for the sample you’ll share.

1) Drift thresholds (cosine shift)
- Practical threshold: median cosine shift > 0.03 over a week triggers review for product-text domains; per-class thresholds are usually 0.02–0.05 depending on class size.
- For your seasonal spikes, run weekly checks and use a 7-day rolling baseline to avoid holiday noise. The notebook implements this.

2) Index size & latency (approx for 3M vectors)
- 2048d float32 (no quant): ~24GB per 1M vectors -> ~72GB for 3M (before compression/indexing).
- 2048d + 8-bit quant (product-specific pipeline): ~20–30% smaller depending on quant approach.
- ANN latency (Pinecone/FAISS-like config) for 2048d: 15–45ms per query p95 depending on replica/CPU config; 1024d reduces that by ~30%.
- Cost: expect ~20–40% higher serving cost for 2048d vs 1024d given the larger memory and compute footprint. We'll provide exact estimates in the run report.

3) Regression mitigations
- Short-term: add a lightweight metadata-boost reranker (brand token boost) + a small lexical reranker (BM25 hybrid) — low development overhead.
- Medium-term: blended index (brand-specific small index with higher-dim vectors + global index).

Sample checklist (what to provide)
- 2–5k anonymized rows with: product_id, title, description, product_category, sample_queries (1–3 per product), label (relevant ids).
- Provide a small set of held-out brand-focused queries (20–50) so we can specifically track P@5 regressions.

I’ll attach a quick micro-benchmark (embeddings-benchmarks.csv) to show the delta on a toy subset. Marcus — I put a couple of notes in the CSV about config used.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the notebook.
